comparator.academicYear: Current UvA published bachelor curriculum, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official curriculum totals 60+60+60=180 EC. The generic target offers five second-year core-module specialisations. International Relations is selected by the neutral official-order tie-break, before UCR course selection. The first-listed Sustainability Politics option is likewise used for the 6-EC year-2 restricted elective. Year 3 preserves the published seminar and thesis choices plus 30 EC of genuinely open elective/minor/internship/exchange space. The English and bilingual tracks have identical content.

routeSelection.basis: The generic bachelor has five official core-module specialisations and none is identified as the broad default. alternatives.label: Political institutions, democracy & social change
alternatives.concept: Combines comparative politics, political thought, international relations, law, sociology, communication and research methods to analyse power, institutions, democracy, inequality and political change. It is the broadest and closest feasible UCR response to the UvA degree.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed plan balances political institutions and theory with society, law, international politics, communication and empirical inquiry.
progression: Political, sociological, legal and methods foundations precede advanced comparative politics, conflict, EU politics, social theory and communication. All prerequisites and offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: International relations, conflict & global governance
alternatives.concept: Develops the official International Relations specialisation through international theory, security, conflict, international law, human rights, empires, sustainability governance, youth radicalisation and peace-building.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum gives sustained weight to interstate relations, international law, conflict, security, global institutions and peace.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest plan, this route replaces political communication, constitutional comparison and some domestic social-change courses with international history, criminal justice, security, human rights and conflict-oriented psychology. Six courses differ and the organising question becomes international conflict and governance.
progression: Politics, sociology, philosophy and law foundations precede international theory, conflict, advanced law, global governance and research. All prerequisites and offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Public policy, political economy & governance
alternatives.concept: Builds from the official Public Policy and Governance and Political Economy directions, combining national institutions, comparative government, public economics, macro- and microeconomics, econometrics, law, data and policy communication.
alternatives.labelReason: The plan centres how governments make, finance, communicate and evaluate policy under economic and institutional constraints.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces much of the closest and international-conflict curricula with economics, econometrics, data science, public administration, national political communication and policy research. It differs from each earlier plan by well over 30 EC and prioritises governance and policy evaluation.
progression: Political, historical, legal, economic, data and methods foundations precede public economics, econometrics, advanced government, communication and independent research. All prerequisites and offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

selection.assessment: The institutions–democracy–social-change plan is the closest broad UCR response. The official International Relations and Public Policy/Political Economy directions support two further coherent and mechanically distinct curricula. All three pass current UCR feasibility checks, so production stops at the maximum of three.

notes.text: The UvA degree provides a compulsory Political Science core, repeated academic-skills and research projects, a formal core-module specialisation, bachelor seminars and a supervised thesis. UCR offers substantial political theory, comparative politics, international relations, law, sociology, economics and methods, but it does not reproduce the same integrated departmental sequence or specialisation structure.
